description: We are YPC Star Squad, a family team of a mother and two young explorers taking part from home in Erode. Our challenge is “Abandoned but not Forgotten”. Our children wrote and painted “Roxy the Great Satellite”, a story for ages 7 to 12 about a made-up Mars robot inspired by NASA’s Opportunity rover. Our slides add real NASA facts about silent explorers on Mars and the Moon. Our team is complete, so we are not looking for more members.
summary: Roxy the Great Satellite is a story for children aged 7 to 12 that brings a forgotten robot explorer back to life. Two young explorers wrote it by hand and painted every page, guided by their mother. Roxy is a made-up Mars robot who looks for water, takes samples, sends photos and shares her solar panel with astronauts in need. Her ending comes from real history: NASA’s Opportunity rover worked on Mars for about 14 years until a planet-wide dust storm blocked its sunlight in 2018. Our 7 slides and full story PDF turn that real mission into a story children can feel, with real NASA facts about Opportunity, Spirit, Ingenuity and the Apollo 15 Falcon lander.
details:
This is our first project as a family.

Why we chose this challenge: NASA has left rovers, landers and helicopters on the Moon and Mars. Children hear about the active missions, but rarely about the machines whose work is finished. We wanted children to meet them as characters, not as a list of dates.

What we made: A hand-written, hand-painted story called Roxy the Great Satellite. The children came up with the idea, wrote the story and painted every page. Roxy is a cheerful, made-up robot who explores Mars. She looks for water, takes samples, sends photos, and gives her solar panel to astronauts who need help. The moral is that sharing is better than selfishness. The story ends with an amazing fact: a storm once blocked a real robot’s sunlight on Mars, and that robot is still in the same place today.

How the real science fits in: Roxy is made up, and we say so clearly. Her ending is inspired by NASA’s Opportunity rover, so our slides tell the real story: about 14 years on Mars, 45.16 km driven, confirmation that water stayed on Mars for a long time, and a last message on June 10, 2018, during a planet-wide dust storm. We also introduce three more silent explorers: Spirit, the Ingenuity helicopter and the Apollo 15 Falcon lander on the Moon. Every real fact comes from the NASA pages in our references, and we checked each one.

Who it helps: School-age and casual space fans, ages 7 to 12. The slides use large, clear text and every picture on them has a text description. The story PDF includes a typed copy of the children’s words, with their own spelling, so it is easy to read.

What we hope to achieve: We want children to feel a personal connection to the machines NASA left behind, and to see that a story can be a friendly way into science.

Honest notes: The children made the story. An AI assistant (Claude) helped with the slide layout, the typed copy and organising our fact notes. The idea, story, handwriting and paintings are the children’s own work, guided by their mother.

Tools: Paper, Paints and Pens, a Phone camera, Google Slides and Google Drive.
